Lessons.Title: Continuity
ExplanationParagraphs: Continuity at a requires f(a) defined, limit exists, and limit equals f(a).
Discontinuities include removable holes, finite jumps and infinite asymptotes.
For piecewise functions check left and right formulas and assigned boundary value.
Polynomial functions continuous everywhere; rational functions wherever denominator nonzero.
The intermediate value theorem applies to functions continuous on a closed interval.
Independent Cool-down: evaluate a representative local example and explain the limiting or derivative reasoning.

WorkedExamples.Title: Identifying Discontinuities
WorkedExamples.Question: Find discontinuity of f(x)=(x²−9)/(x−3) (unredefined).
WorkedExamples.Method: Use source-family limit, continuity or derivative definition.
Steps: Removable at x=3; limit=6 but function undefined there.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Removable at x=3; limit=6 but function undefined there.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify domain, one-sided values or difference quotient.

WorkedExamples.Title: Determining Whether a Piecewise Function is Continuous at a Given Number
WorkedExamples.Question: For f(x)=x+4 if x<0, and x+3 if x≥0, continuous at0?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use source-family limit, continuity or derivative definition.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify domain, one-sided values or difference quotient.

WorkedExamples.Title: Determining Whether a Rational Function is Continuous at a Given Number
WorkedExamples.Question: At x→5, g(x)=1/(x−5) has which continuity type?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use source-family limit, continuity or derivative definition.
Steps: Infinite discontinuity, opposite-sign unbounded one-sided limits.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Infinite discontinuity, opposite-sign unbounded one-sided limits.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify domain, one-sided values or difference quotient.

WorkedExamples.Title: Determining the Input Values for Which a Piecewise Function Is Discontinuous
WorkedExamples.Question: Define f(x)=x² for x≠6, f(6)=37. Is it continuous at x=6?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use source-family limit, continuity or derivative definition.
Steps: No, removable point mismatch: limit=36, value=37.
WorkedExamples.Answer: No, removable point mismatch: limit=36, value=37.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify domain, one-sided values or difference quotient.

WorkedExamples.Title: Determining Whether a Piecewise Function Is Continuous
WorkedExamples.Question: Does continuous f(x)=x³−7 on interval[0,8] have a zero by IVT?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use source-family limit, continuity or derivative definition.
Steps: Yes, f(0)<0 and f(a+1)>0, so some c satisfies f(c)=0.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Yes, f(0)<0 and f(a+1)>0, so some c satisfies f(c)=0.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify domain, one-sided values or difference quotient.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Substitute directly into0/0 or assume a hole changes approached limit.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Limit concerns nearby behavior, not isolated point value.
